title: Increment Field

children:
This field determines how the system will increment locations when it 
 creates a location range.

When the system increments numeric locations, it increments through 
 all positions in the location number.

In the example below, the location range includes two aisles. Each aisle 
 has two bays; each bay is three levels high. To obtain a location number 
 for each location in these aisles, you would provide the following increment 
 value: 001-001-001. As the values in the Locations Created column illustrate, 
 the system will increment across number positions.

Note: if you select an increment other than 001, the system will increment 
 by that value. For example, if you incremented by 001-001-002, the system 
 would have created 'every other location: 001-001-001, 001-001-003, etc. 
 In this case, it would skip all even numbered levels.

When the system increments alpha locations, it increments by position 
 only. This minimizes setup errors and decreases the likelihood that you 
 will generate too many locations.

In the example below, the location range includes three shelves. Each 
 shelf has three bays. To obtain a location name for each location in these 
 shelves, you would provide the following increment value: 11. As the values 
 in the Locations Created column illustrate, the system will

increment across number positions. Once it reaches the last letter in 
 the ending location sequence, it attempts to create new locations using 
 the next starting location letter.
